objective.text: Understand why default test-environment CSRF bypass can conceal missing token behavior.

difficulty.rationale: Avoid interpreting an intentionally bypassed framework test path as evidence of token enforcement.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A standard HTTP test runs in the testing environment and a tokenless protected POST succeeds. The team claims this proves token validation is broken in production. What must a focused enforcement test account for?

options.text: Asserting that the middleware class appears in the source file is sufficient to prove enforcement.
options.rationale: Class presence does not exercise the runtime decision or a failing token path.
options.misconception: Class presence does not exercise the runtime decision or a failing token path.

options.text: Changing only Accept to application/json forces CSRF enforcement during ordinary testing.
options.rationale: Accept controls response preference, not the unit-test bypass condition.
options.misconception: Accept controls response preference, not the unit-test bypass condition.

options.text: Tokenless success proves the middleware is disabled in every environment.
options.rationale: The middleware explicitly considers the environment, so this observation cannot support that global conclusion.
options.misconception: The middleware explicitly considers the environment, so this observation cannot support that global conclusion.

options.text: The middleware bypasses its check in the normal console testing context; exercise a controlled non-bypass path and explicit origin/token conditions.
options.rationale: A test-environment success can reflect the documented bypass, not production enforcement. Laravel 13 origin acceptance must also be controlled.

explanation.summary: A test-environment success can reflect the documented bypass, not production enforcement. Laravel 13 origin acceptance must also be controlled.
